content:
- Overestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially strong negative sentiment), especially in early forecast periods.  
- Underestimate prices when sentiment turns positive or is mildly positive, particularly after recent spikes.  
- Overshoot after sharp upward sentiment spikes; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to model peak.  
- Mean-revert forecasts toward recent 7–14 day average if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.  
- Avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment swings; lag sentiment effects by 2–3 days in forecast adjustments.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, reduce forecast slope downward by 10–15% from baseline.  
- If forecast exceeds true outcome by >5% in 3 consecutive days, adjust downward by 1–2% per day until convergence.
